---
title: Headless uploads and Uppy
description: Drive uploads from your own interface with the ClipMuxUpload class, or from any client through the upload routes.
---

When you want your own upload interface, use the class inside
`<clipmux-uploader>` directly: `ClipMuxUpload` from `@clipmux/uploader`. It
sends a file in parts straight to storage, resumes from what storage holds,
retries, and reports progress, and leaves every pixel to you. For anything
else, such as a native app or another upload library, the upload routes are
a small API of their own.

## Before you start

- A backend route that creates uploads: the `upload` callback of
  `clipmuxHandler`, or your own route calling `POST /v1/uploads`. See
  [Your backend route](/docs/build/upload/browser#your-backend-route).
- `npm i @clipmux/uploader`.

## Upload with ClipMuxUpload

Give it the file and your `createUrl`, the same route the element uses:

```ts
import { ClipMuxUpload, ClipMuxUploadError } from '@clipmux/uploader'

const upload = new ClipMuxUpload(file, {
  createUrl: '/api/clipmux/upload?lesson=42',
  onProgress: (p) => setProgress(p.bytesUploaded / p.bytesTotal),
})

try {
  const asset = await upload.start() // the video, processing
  console.log(asset.id)
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof ClipMuxUploadError) console.log(err.code, err.status, err.retryable)
}
```

`start()` POSTs `{size, name, type}` to `createUrl` with the page's cookies,
remembers the upload in `localStorage` so a reload resumes it, sends the
parts and completes the upload. Calling `start()` again after a rejection
continues from what storage holds.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `start()` | Uploads what storage doesn't hold yet and completes the upload. Resolves with the video. |
| `pause()` | Stops sending. Parts already stored stay. |
| `resume()` | Continues after `pause()`. |
| `cancel()` | Stops for good and tells ClipMux. The video becomes `errored` with `upload_cancelled`. |
| `upload` | The upload in use, once there is one. |

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createUrl` | | Your backend route that creates the upload. Give this or `upload`. |
| `upload` | | An upload your backend already created: the body of `POST /v1/uploads`. |
| `endpoint` | the upload's `endpoint` | Your ClipMux server's URL, if the upload doesn't carry it. |
| `store` | `localStorage` | Where a `createUrl` upload is remembered until it completes; `null` forgets it on reload. |
| `concurrency` | `4` | Parts in flight at once. |
| `maxAttempts` | `6` | Tries per request before giving up. |
| `onProgress` | | Called with `{ bytesUploaded, bytesTotal, partsDone, partsTotal }`. |
| `signal` | | An `AbortSignal` that stops the upload. |

A failure rejects with a `ClipMuxUploadError` with `code`, `status` and
`retryable`, and leaves the upload resumable for 24 hours. Codes include
`create_denied` (your route answered `401` or `403`), `network`,
`etag_not_exposed`, and the API's own codes such as `too_large`.

## With an upload your backend created

If your backend creates the upload some other way, for example as part of
saving a form, pass the body with `upload` and the server URL with
`endpoint`. `rememberUpload` keeps it across a reload:

```ts
import { ClipMuxUpload, rememberUpload } from '@clipmux/uploader'

const memory = rememberUpload(localStorage)
const created = memory.load(file) ?? (await createUploadOnMyBackend(file.size))
memory.save(file, created)

const asset = await new ClipMuxUpload(file, {
  upload: created,
  endpoint: 'https://video.example.com',
}).start()
memory.forget(file)
```

Only the upload's ID, token and part layout are stored; ClipMux itself knows
which parts it holds. `clipmux.uploads.create` in `@clipmux/node` returns
the body with `endpoint` added, so the browser needs no other setting.

## The upload routes, for any client

`ClipMuxUpload` is a thin client of four routes. Any client that can make
HTTP requests can do the same, as
[Your first video with curl](/docs/build/first-video) does by hand.

| Step | Route | Credential |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create the upload; get `upload_id`, `part_size`, `part_count` and `upload_token`. | `POST /v1/uploads` | Your API key, from your backend |
| Sign up to 100 part URLs, each good for an hour. | `POST /v1/uploads/{id}/parts` | The upload token |
| `PUT` each part's bytes to its URL; keep the `ETag` header. | The signed URL | None |
| On resume, list the parts storage holds. | `GET /v1/uploads/{id}/parts` | The upload token |
| Complete with every part's number and `ETag`. | `POST /v1/uploads/{id}/complete` | The upload token |
| Or cancel. | `POST /v1/uploads/{id}/cancel` | The upload token, or your API key |

Every part is exactly `part_size` bytes (32 MiB) except the last, and the
parts must number `part_count`. Upload-token requests are limited to 10 a
second per upload. Storage must expose `ETag` to a browser page.

## Uppy

There is no Uppy plugin for ClipMux. ClipMux's upload routes are its own,
not S3's API, and ClipMux never hands a browser S3 credentials or signs
arbitrary S3 requests, so Uppy's S3 plugin can't talk to them as it is. To
keep Uppy's interface, wire its upload step to `ClipMuxUpload`, or to the
routes above, yourself. Either way, test it against your server: ClipMux
doesn't test any Uppy release.

## Check it works

Upload a short file and watch `onProgress` reach `bytesTotal`. `start()`
resolves with a video whose `status` is `processing`. Reload halfway
through and start again with the same file: progress jumps to the parts
already stored.

- `create_invalid`: your `createUrl` route answered without an upload.
- `file_mismatch`: the file isn't the one the upload was created for (its
  size gives a different number of parts).
- `part_url_rejected`: storage refused a part URL twice; check the server's
  public URL and storage settings.
